title: Shifted-unit cup transpose under a monoidal adjunction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be additive monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with biadditive tensor, units $I_{\mathcal C},I_{\mathcal D}$, and additive integer shifts with specified zero-shift and shift-addition isomorphisms. Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $F:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be additive adjoints $L\dashv F$. Suppose $L$ is strong monoidal, with inverse tensor comparison $t_{X,Y}:L(X\otimes Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}LX\otimes LY$ and unit comparison $\ell:LI_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{\mathcal D}$, and both functors have fixed shift comparisons for which the adjunction unit and counit commute with shifts. Write $S_n^{\mathcal C}=I_{\mathcal C}[-n]$ and $S_n^{\mathcal D}=I_{\mathcal D}[-n]$. Choose isomorphisms $r^{\mathcal C}_{p,q}:S^{\mathcal C}_{p+q}\to S^{\mathcal C}_p\otimes S^{\mathcal C}_q$ and $r^{\mathcal D}_{p,q}$ of the same type, identified by $L$, $t$, $\ell$ and the fixed shift comparisons.

Give $F$ the lax monoidal structure $(e,\mu)$ adjoint to $(\ell,t)$, and put $C=FI_{\mathcal D}$ and $M=F(m)\mu_{I_{\mathcal D},I_{\mathcal D}}$, where $m:I_{\mathcal D}\otimes I_{\mathcal D}\to I_{\mathcal D}$ is unit multiplication. Then $(C,M,e)$ is an associative unital algebra object, and the unit and counit of this adjunction are monoidal for these structures. If $\varepsilon:LF\to1$ is the counit, the precise normalization is
$$\varepsilon_{U\otimes V}L(\mu_{U,V})=(\varepsilon_U\otimes\varepsilon_V)t_{FU,FV},\qquad \varepsilon_{I_{\mathcal D}}L(e)=\ell.$$
For $x:I_{\mathcal D}\to I_{\mathcal D}[p]$, write $f=x[-p]:S_p^{\mathcal D}\to I_{\mathcal D}$ using shift addition, and let $\Phi_p(x):S_p^{\mathcal C}\to C$ be its adjoint under $LS_p^{\mathcal C}\cong S_p^{\mathcal D}$. Define $a\smile b=M(a\otimes b)r^{\mathcal C}_{p,q}$. Then $\Phi_0(1)=e$ under the zero-shift identifications. For every $p,q\in\mathbf Z$, $x:I_{\mathcal D}\to I_{\mathcal D}[p]$ and $y:I_{\mathcal D}\to I_{\mathcal D}[q]$, the transpose of $\Phi_p(x)\smile\Phi_q(y)$, transported along $LS^{\mathcal C}_{p+q}\cong S^{\mathcal D}_{p+q}$, is exactly
$$m\bigl(x[-p]\otimes y[-q]\bigr)r^{\mathcal D}_{p,q}.$$
The order of the two factors is as displayed; the assertion applies to arbitrary morphisms of these categories.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates] to $(\ell,t)$ to obtain the specified lax structure on $F$. Its unit is the adjoint of $\ell$. By [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit] the adjunction unit and counit are monoidal. The tensor equation for the monoidal counit is $\varepsilon_{U\otimes V}\circ L(\mu_{U,V})\circ t_{FU,FV}^{-1}=\varepsilon_U\otimes\varepsilon_V$; compose on the right with $t_{FU,FV}$ to get the first normalization. Its unit equation is $\varepsilon_{I_{\mathcal D}}\circ L(e)\circ\ell^{-1}=1_{I_{\mathcal D}}$; compose with $\ell$ to get the second. These are precisely the composite lax structures in the cited statement.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-tensor-unit-monoid] in $\mathcal D$. Transport its monoid $(I_{\mathcal D},m,1)$ through the lax monoidal functor $F$ by clause 1 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport]. The resulting multiplication is $F(m)\circ\mu_{I_{\mathcal D},I_{\mathcal D}}=M$, and its unit is $F(1)\circ e=e$. Thus $(C,M,e)$ is associative and unital.

proof.text: Write $h_n:LS_n^{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_n^{\mathcal D}$ for the prescribed unit/shift comparison. The assumed compatibility of $r$ means exactly $(h_p\otimes h_q)\circ t_{S_p^{\mathcal C},S_q^{\mathcal C}}\circ L(r^{\mathcal C}_{p,q})=r^{\mathcal D}_{p,q}\circ h_{p+q}$. Put $a=\Phi_p(x)$, $b=\Phi_q(y)$, $f=x[-p]$, $g=y[-q]$. By the inverse Hom-bijection formula in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], $\varepsilon_I\circ L(a)=f\circ h_p$ and $\varepsilon_I\circ L(b)=g\circ h_q$, where $I=I_{\mathcal D}$.

proof.text: Expand the transpose $T=\varepsilon_I\circ L(M\circ(a\otimes b)\circ r^{\mathcal C}_{p,q})$ using [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Counit naturality for $m$ gives $\varepsilon_I\circ L(F(m))=m\circ\varepsilon_{I\otimes I}$. Hence the tensor normalization of step 1 gives $T=m\circ(\varepsilon_I\otimes\varepsilon_I)\circ t_{C,C}\circ L(a\otimes b)\circ L(r^{\mathcal C}_{p,q})$. Naturality of $t$ rewrites this as $m\circ((\varepsilon_I\circ L(a))\otimes(\varepsilon_I\circ L(b)))\circ t_{S_p^{\mathcal C},S_q^{\mathcal C}}\circ L(r^{\mathcal C}_{p,q})$. Substitute the two adjoint equations and the compatibility equation of step 3: $T=m\circ(f\otimes g)\circ r^{\mathcal D}_{p,q}\circ h_{p+q}$. Precompose with $h_{p+q}^{-1}$ to obtain the stated transported transpose. Every operation preserves the displayed factor order; no symmetry, generators, or degree restriction is used.

proof.text: For $p=0$, under the specified zero-shift identifications, $f=1_I$ and $h_0=\ell$. Thus $\Phi_0(1)$ is the adjoint of $\ell$, which is $e$ by the unit formula of [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates]. This also covers zero objects and zero morphisms; the calculation in step 4 applies to all integers $p,q$.
